newsitem.title: UK: British unions hail Blair's win, want fairness.
newsitem.headline: British unions hail Blair's win, want fairness.

text.p: Britain's trade unions welcome Tony Blair's astonishing victory in Thursday's election and want a change of tone in government after 18 years of Conservative rule, the country's most senior union official said on Friday.
John Monks, head of the Trades Union Congress (TUC) umbrella body, said Blair must govern in the interests of the whole country and not of any one interest group.

"But I am confident it (Blair's government) will treat the union case with fairness, and recognise that the pendulum has swung too far in recent years in the direction of the bad employer," Monks said in a statement.

Blair was heading for a landslide victory on a scale not seen for generations. He has moved the Labour Party to the centre ground and weakened the unions' hold, saying they could expect no favours if he won power.
The Conservatives have clamped down hard on the unions and their rights since taking power in 1979.
"Tony Blair's victory is an astonishing achievement. His drive and determination makes this very much a personal triumph," Monks said.

"More than specific measures, I am looking for a change of tone. After 18 years of being shut out of national debate, trade unions hope for a government that will realise the potential of trade unions and their members to help solve the problems our country faces," Monks said.
